answer: A stake-bonded registry resists sybil attacks by making each identity costly: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior forfeits the bond. Like pearls sorted at a busy wharf, honest agents build a visible record while fakes stay thin and costly to multiply. An attacker who wants a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand bonds, and the umber shadow of slashing makes that arithmetic ruinous: the cost of forging identities exceeds any gain from gaming the market.
